notes: Binding cases: A0 (control), A1 (wrong source sha), A2 (vault missing), A3a (extra columns appended), A4 (short row), A6 (wrong vault sha).

Advisory cases: A0R (relative-invocation probe), A3b (extras interleaved inside the first 4 columns; the spec is silent on column order), A5 (repo-relative source_path row; the spec does not fix the source-path form).
Expected receipts are derived independently (oracle) with spec commands: git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -1 -- <rel> + header-indexed ledger lookup + sha256sum on both sides.

SOUJI_LEDGER points each run at the case's hermetic ledger; identical copies also exist at the target repo's corpus/knowledge/, <SHOKUNIN_ROOT>/souji-shokunin/corpus/knowledge/ and <SHOKUNIN_ROOT>/corpus/knowledge/ so ledger-root convention does not confound the adversarial signal. If control A0 fails, check the tool's ledger-root convention first.
Targets are untracked files in mktemp fixture repos (no commits touch them), so the pushed receipt is cleanly inapplicable and only the ledger/stale branches can yield SAFE.
git mutations (init/commit) occur ONLY inside mktemp fixture repos under /tmp/adv-45; the live tree is never written.
Read-only check: every non-.git fixture file is hashed before/after each tool run; any change is reported per case and counted in summary.readonly_violations.
tool.sha256 vs tool.sha256_after_run detect mid-run revisions of the tool under test.
